Rule 5, fixed signatures keep their shape: public methods of top-level lib/Service/*.php classes, lib/Kernel/Contracts, lib/Contract, events, IFlowNode, IMcpToolProvider, and classes other Conduction apps name (ObjectService, FileService, ConfigurationService, OrganisationService, SchemaMapper, RegisterMapper, AuditTrailMapper, MagicMapper, TransitionEngine, CredentialBrokerService, and any class found by `gh api -X GET search/code -f q='org:ConductionNL <ClassName>' --jq '.items[].repository.full_name'` in another repo) keep their signatures: add the value-object method beside it and make the old one build the object and delegate in at most 5 lines; controller route actions keep their route parameters (the dispatcher binds by name), build ObjectRef or ListQuery on the first line and delegate.

RULE 4, TWO-PARAMETER CONSTRUCTORS (ADR-011, accepted; this is the point of wave R and part of your target): an autowired class (service, handler, mapper, listener, job, command, repair step, MCP tool, middleware) takes AT MOST 2 constructor parameters. WHAT TO DO, in this order: 1) controller constructors to `(IRequest $request, <Name>ControllerServices $services)` (Rule 4; `parent::__construct(Application::APP_ID, $request)`; AppHost's generic controllers that serve another app's id are exempt); access guards stay direct constructor parameters, so a controller that injects a guard keeps it beside the bundle and says so in the PR. 2) Other constructors, under RULE 4 below: every autowired constructor in your files goes to at most 2 parameters (more than 4 first, then 3 and 4); a class that injects RegisterMapperInterface, SchemaMapperInterface and MagicMapperInterface (or two of them plus a need for the third) takes SchemaCatalogInterface instead; a constructor that only stores its parameters gets promoted properties and an empty body. Update every place that builds the class (tests, factories); a registrar or *Wiring file in YOUR OWNED FILES is yours to change for this; lib/AppInfo is never yours; a class built by hand in a file you do not own stays as it is and goes in LEFT. Use the pattern the unit list names (Rule 1 shared object, Rule 2 operation or Options object, Rule 3 run object, Rule 5 facade); drop a parameter that is unused or derivable (the schema when the object carries it, the register when the schema names it); move a method onto the data it uses; split a bool flag into two named methods. The hint after each unit below comes from the design simulation; follow the ADR where they disagree.
RULES: no option arrays (including a new `array $options` that absorbs parameters), no variadics, no passing IRequest below a controller, no moving values to a mutable field on a shared service, no value object that mirrors one method's parameter list under a generic name (FooArgs, BarParams), no generic Context bag. Helpers you extract take at most 2 parameters; keep new units at cc <= 5 and <= 15 lines. The guard flags `_rbac` and `_multitenancy` stay named parameters wherever they appear today (call-site tooling and the IDOR gate read them by name): never fold them into a value object, an Options object or a run object. A unit whose parameters cannot drop without breaking a Rule 5 signature is thinned to a delegate of at most 5 lines and listed in LEFT (a).
OUT OF SCOPE THIS ROUND (do not start them, even partly): entity read-interfaces (no new interfaces for Db entities, no type-hint swap from entities to interfaces), the lib/Db boundary phase (no classes moved between lib/Db and lib/Service, no Db-owned ports replacing Service types), and moving RBAC SQL out of lib/Db. Skip files in open PRs outside this round (gh api 'repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=100&page=N' for N=1,2,3... until a page is empty, then /pulls/<n>/files?per_page=100&page=N the same way; never --paginate); re-check before starting each class.
STRICT TYPES: keep every moved body in a file with the same declare(strict_types) mode as its source (a non-strict body moved into a strict file turns coercion into TypeError). New bundle/parameter classes may be strict only if every value they receive is already typed.
TESTS FIRST: before refactoring a unit with no test that pins its outcomes, add a characterisation test on the OLD code (commit it first in the PR) covering each branch you touch; it must still pass after. No clock-pinned or date/PHP-build-dependent goldens.
ACCESS CODE (RBAC, tenancy, purpose, audit, locks, delete guards, retention, personal data) is in scope but: never change allowed/refused outcomes; golden test on the OLD code first pinning allowed AND refused outcomes plus one mutation check; a non-array/unexpected value must still be refused where it was refused; checks stay before the operation; _rbac/_multitenancy unchanged. PermissionHandler: use PermissionHandlerInterface.
GUARDS: run tests/Unit/Architecture, tests/Unit/Contract, tests/Unit/Kernel, tests/Unit/Service/Rules, tests/Unit/Controller/ControllerServicesWiringTest.php and ControllerSessionWiringTest.php, tests/Unit/Architecture/Adr011ValueObjectRulesTest.php, plus tests of touched classes (vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit.xml --no-coverage <paths>) ON YOUR BRANCH MERGED WITH CURRENT origin/main (several guards read source: allowed callers of a class, who calls ->record(), which bundle a controller keeps). Never edit or weaken a guard or shared test helper/fixture; guard allowlists may only shrink; if a guard lists allowed callers of a concrete class, follow it. php -l, phpcs, phpstan on touched files. Add no new @SuppressWarnings, typed props assigned one by one, no list destructuring into props, PHPUnit calls positional, license headers on new files. Bugs/security issues you find: separate "fix: ..." PR with a failing-then-passing test, no exploit details in text.
SETUP: composer as in ROUND 12 BASE above. Check push early: git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/cloud/r01-probe; if refused, call add_repo owner ConductionNL repo openregister access push. Foreground only, never end your turn while waiting, no routines, no reminders, never poll CI.
COMMIT AND PUSH OFTEN (the point Ruben stressed): after every coherent step (test added, class changed, guards green) commit and `git push origin HEAD:cloud/r01-<topic>`, at least every 20 minutes of work, so a session end loses nothing. Add new untracked files explicitly (`git add <path>`; `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists them): `git add -u` silently drops new files. Pushing to your own branch is safe while it has no open PR; the moment its PR is open, the branch is finished.
ACCESS TITLE: any PR that moves access logic or touches an access path (a path matching lib/.../(Rbac|Audit|Archival|Retention|Party|Organisation|Tenancy|Purpose|Consent|Share|Lock|Gdpr|Avg), or any change to _rbac, _multitenancy, permissions, grants, tenancy, ownership, purpose, retention, consent, locks, delete guards) has a title starting exactly `[access]`, for example `[access] refactor(rbac): ...`. When in doubt, use the prefix.
MEASURE (the only count that decides anything): git fetch origin refs/heads/sig-lane-briefs/r12r && rm -rf /tmp/lm && mkdir -p /tmp/lm && git archive FETCH_HEAD sig-measure | tar -x -C /tmp/lm; python3 /tmp/lm/sig-measure/lane_measure.py --app . --lane R01 --scopes /tmp/lm/sig-measure/scopes.json. If you still cannot run it, write "measurement not run" in your final message: a home-made counter does not count, and lanes that used one reported numbers the tree did not show.
LESSONS FROM REVIEW (hit #7380, #7361, #7373 in round 11): a constructor change is not finished until every test and every named-argument factory that builds that class follows it. Grep for the class name in tests/ and in the registrars and wiring classes, and run the tests of every touched directory, not only the mirrored test class. Goldens never depend on the timezone or the clock: inject or freeze time and never pin a local time. Leave an existing @SuppressWarnings in place when moving code unless the warning is really gone. Never edit tests/unit/support/*. Access guards stay direct constructor parameters, never bundled into an aggregate or a Services bundle.
DELIVERY: as many PRs as the scope takes, there is no limit per lane. Each PR stays small and reviewable: at most 10 classes and about 400 changed production lines per PR, one coherent topic. OPENING A PR: open a PR only when the branch is finished, never as a draft: the merge pipeline (cloud-list) batches every open cloud/* PR, so an open PR must be complete, merged with current origin/main, and past its guards. A PR is FINISHED when opened: never push more commits to an open PR; further work goes on a new branch and a new PR. Each PR from a fresh branch `cloud/r01-<topic>` off origin/main (lane id R01, branch prefix lowercase r01), merged (never rebased) with current origin/main before opening. Conventional commits with only the trailer `Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5-5`: no Co-Authored-By, no Signed-off-by. Open via gh api repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls -f title -f head -f base=main -f body (what changed, what ran, before/after numbers for your area, which ADR-011 rule each change applies, AI disclosed). Never open a draft. Don't merge. Never touch main or another lane's cloud/* branch. Never rebase, force-push or skip hooks. Finish with the FINAL MESSAGE below.
FINAL MESSAGE (always, also when you stop early): (1) the before, target and now numbers from MEASURE; (2) your PR numbers; (3) LEFT: every item still over the limit (file and unit) with its reason; (4) when you could not finish, a line starting `HAND-OFF:` with the pushed branch name and the head commit, and the exact remaining files. If your context or session is running out, stop starting new classes, finish and push the one in hand, and write this message: a lane that stops without it is invisible to the coordinator.
